I recently ordered 4 bottles of Mintop 120 ml from Red Rose Chemist. Although they were initially out of stock, they arranged it for me. However, they sent me 60 ml bottles but billed me for 120 ml bottles. When I reordered, I noticed the discrepancy and immediately informed them, providing the bill, the boxes, and proof of payment via GPay. This experience has left me feeling cheated. Be cautious and double-check your orders with them—they appear to be dishonest.

featured_reviews.name: Jaya Kanoria
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yesterday I went to Alankar Chemist with a typed and printed very clear prescription for an eye ointment - Talimus .03%.
They gave me .1%.
Alankar being a reputed shop, I did not check this before putting one drop in each eye that night.
At 2 am my eyes began to radiate heat. In the morning they were swollen and hot. I washed them thoroughly and scrubbed the skin around them.
At 11 am, I reached the doctor. He asked me to put cold compresses on my eyes but this gives only temporary relief. My eyes are still burning.
I let Alankar Chemist know what happened. On Alankar’s request, I sent a picture of the prescription on Whatsapp. They replied saying that if I confirmed with the Dr, they would give me the correct medicine! I said there was clearly no need for confirmation. I then sent my person across. They CHARGED him for the new tube and demanded the old (used) tube back. Hence this review. Never trust a chemist - always check what they are giving you
